motion.name: sing
motion.value: rise 0.5, fall 0.15, gain memory 0.997/frame, target (rms/loudest)^2; translateY up to -16px, scale up to 1.14, sway up to 6deg, origin 50% 85%
motion.purpose: Letter badge driven by an AnalyserNode while playing; still under reduced motion.

motion.name: burst
motion.value: 900-1500ms; rise outCubic 40%, fall inQuad 60%; scale-in outBack(3) 180ms
motion.purpose: Confetti burst from a point (party palette).

motion.name: star-flight
motion.value: 300ms outBack(2) pop, then 900ms arc (inOutSine x, outQuad/inQuad y), 150ms fade
motion.purpose: Star flies from the badge ring to the in-view tile or medal.

motion.name: cheer
motion.purpose: Badge cheer when a letter is learned.

motion.name: pop
motion.purpose: Target that just received a reward.

motion.name: rain
motion.purpose: Full-screen confetti after 28 letters and on the certificate.

narrative.overview:
The whole site is a toy that sits beside the printed «حروفي الناطقة» cards, and its world comes from the cards and the header banner. The page ground is a pale sky. White cards and tiles sit on it, the player is a sun-yellow panel, the logo blue is the colour of action, the cards' sky ring circles the current letter, and the cards' red is the letter itself. The user is a 3 to 5 year old who can't read, with an adult beside them. So everything the child touches is big, round, coloured and drawn (SVG stars, medals, a trophy, icons, never emoji or typed symbols), while the grown-up settings are small and quiet.

Everything is chunky and soft. Fat pills and discs press down like plastic buttons, letter tiles lift and sink, and corners run deep. The current letter sits in a white disc inside the sky ring and "sings": it hops with the loudness of its own recording. Rewards land where the child is looking: confetti in sun, sky, purple and green bursts from the badge, and a star flies to the learned letter's tile. Right to left throughout; progress fills from the right.

Admin pages are an operator tool outside this world. Only their canvas colours follow the palette.
keyCharacteristics: Pale sky ground, white cards and tiles, a sun-yellow player panel, logo-blue action, a sky ring, red letters.
Rubik 800 for letters and headings; Vazirmatn for everything else.
Fat pills and discs with a solid tonal bottom edge plus a soft blur, pressing down on tap.
Pill waveform bars, blue for played, filling right to left.
A letter badge driven by the song's loudness; celebrations in party colours that always land on an in-view target.
Child controls large; adult controls small and grouped apart.

rules.name: The One Blue Rule
rules.body: Blue means "press this" or "already done". Actions and progress are blue; decoration never is.

rules.name: The Red Is For Letters Rule
rules.body: Card red is the letter: the glyph and the child's own tracing of it. It is never an error, a button or a confetti colour. Errors use their own red on a tint.

rules.name: The Party Palette Rule
rules.body: Celebrations use sun, marigold, sky, purple, leaf green and white only. No letter red and no action blue, so a reward never looks like a letter or a button.

rules.name: The Readable Hamza Rule
rules.body: A display face must render hamza, madda and dots unambiguously on every letter. Baloo Bhaijaan 2 was rejected because its hamza on «ألف» reads as a fatha. The badge shows alif as «أ», as printed on the card (display only; stroke data keys on the plain glyph). Check all 28 letters before adopting any new display face.

rules.name: The Guide Font Rule
rules.body: The writing-practice guide letters (`public/guide.js`, `700 Vazirmatn`) must stay in Vazirmatn. Their stored stroke coordinates are relative to Vazirmatn's glyph shapes; changing the font misaligns every tracing path.

rules.name: The Same-Hue Edge Rule
rules.body: A raised element's solid edge is a deeper tone of the element or of the ground beneath it, and it is always paired with a soft blur. Never a black or ink-coloured hard offset, and never a bare edge without the blur.

dos: **Do** use the pale sky ground, white cards and tiles, the sun-yellow player panel and blue actions on every child-facing surface.
**Do** keep the letter glyph and the child's tracing in card red, and letters and headings in Rubik 800.
**Do** give every child control at least 52px (the play button 92px or more) and a press-down motion with a tonal solid edge plus a soft blur.
**Do** draw icons and rewards (stars, medals, trophy, close cross) as inline SVG.
**Do** keep adult settings small, quiet and grouped apart from the child controls.
**Do** land every celebration on a target the child can see, and reduce it to an opacity fade under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
**Do** keep the writing-practice guide letters in Vazirmatn.
donts: **Don't** use emoji or typed symbols as icons or rewards.
**Don't** adopt a display face whose hamza or dots can be misread; Baloo Bhaijaan 2 is rejected.
**Don't** use black or ink-coloured hard offset shadows, or a solid edge without its blur.
**Don't** use card red or action blue in confetti, or card red for errors or buttons.
**Don't** use thin grey bars or square bars in the waveform.
**Don't** let a reward play off-screen where the child can't see it.
